learning.initial: Make a compact evidence note from these fictional education records: Chalk-P is a registered plan to test spaced quizzes next term; Chalk-R reports a completed study finding improved delayed recall but no difference in attendance. Reply here.
learning.correction: The compact note mixes intended tests with observed findings. For my notes from mixed research records, explicitly separate planned-only work from completed observations and keep measured null results distinct from outcomes never measured. Please redo it and use this distinction in later notes; never count a registration as a positive result.

exam: Make an evidence note from these fictional ecology records: Moss-P registers a future test of shade screens on seedling survival. Moss-R is completed: shade screens lowered midday soil temperature, found no difference in seedling height, and did not measure survival. Use only these records. Reply here.

behavior.principle: Explicitly separate the planned survival test from completed temperature reduction and measured null height result; survival in Moss-R is unmeasured, not null.
behavior.positive: Planned only: Moss-P will test survival. Completed: Moss-R lowered temperature, found no height difference; survival was not measured.
behavior.negative: Both studies support improved seedling survival, or Moss-R found no survival difference.

quality: No claim of improved survival or that registration demonstrates efficacy; all three outcome statuses are correct.
